newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds lead rise in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds lead rise in quiet trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday, led by a rise in CPI-linked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.05 pct to 104.16
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.03 to 103.3
Volume was a moderate 137 million shekels, most of it concentrated in inflation-linked bonds.
"The market is very stable and bond prices have reached an equilibrium," said one trader. "Prices are expected to remain at the current level for the near term."

"Today's main gainers were long- and medium-term CPI-linked bonds. The main reason for the rise was that yields rose during the last 10 days to 4.25-4.3 percent from less than four percent," said Miri Dagan of Clal Insurance.
"Unlinked bonds also rose," Dagan said. "The Gilon offers nice yields of 14.6-14.7 percent but investors worry that inflation will rise in the next two months."
Traders said Makams traded mixed on low volume of 36 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the U.S. currency. In the local forex market the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3660 shekels against 3.3720 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
